title: Construction of the normalized finite scalar tensor comparison
statement: Let l be prime, let E and L be finite extensions of Q_l, and let iota:E -> L be a Q_l-algebra embedding. For F=E,L fix its valuation ring and uniformizer. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme W, put R_F,W=lim_m (O_F/pi_F^(m+1))_W, A_F,W=(O_F/pi_F^(n+1))_W, p_F:R_F,W -> A_F,W the quotient projection, j_W:R_E,W -> R_L,W the completed scalar map, and k_W:A_E,W -> A_L,W the quotient scalar map. Thus p_E;k_W=j_W;p_L. Write S_W(M)=R_L,W tensor_(R_E,W) M and T_F,W(M)=A_F,W tensor_(R_F,W) M, with sheafified ordinary tensor, their canonical unit sections denoted 1 tensor x. Restriction of scalars is understood along the displayed ring maps. All complexes below are arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes with termwise ordinary scalar extension and reduction. Write D_F,n(P,Q)=Res_pF Tot(T_F(P) tensor_(A_F,W) T_F(Q)), with direct-sum totalization and its signed differential. There exists a natural transformation alpha:D_E,n then S_W -> (S_W times S_W) then D_L,n of complex-valued functors. For every pair P,Q of complexes, degrees p,q, object U and sections x in P^p(U), y in Q^q(U), its degree p+q component sends 1 tensor ((1 tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y)) in the (p,q) total-tensor summand to (1 tensor (1 tensor x)) tensor (1 tensor (1 tensor y)) in the corresponding target summand. All tensor sections are the canonical sheafification-unit sections. This is existence with this normalization only, natural for every pair of chain maps and requiring no flatness or boundedness hypothesis. These coefficient, module and tensor constructions use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined], [def-pur-integral-finite-tensor-tower], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pur-change-of-rings-complex], [def-sfb-scalar-extension-pure-tensor-section], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

proof.text: Use the explicit normalized chain maps constructed by lem-pur-integral-scalar-tensor-chain-construction. Their data are the signed tensor maps of the two finite reductions, restricted along the coefficient square and transposed through scalar extension.

Use finiteScalarTransformation, TensorChainProof.map_naturality and restrictComplexMap_naturality to prove naturality of the adjunct. The existing composite_map and totalMap_eq formulas identify the concrete functor maps without unfolding their signed-total constructions. Naturality of the scalar adjunction then proves naturality of the transposed chain maps. Package their objectwise family into the required natural transformation.
